threads.body: [General] This fallback becomes incorrect after a runtime `SELECT`. A connection created without a `select` URI parameter can execute `SELECT 1`, which leaves `redisUri.select()` null; subsequent commands will now report database 0 even though they run in database 1. Because this instrumentation does not track Vert.x's tainted connection state, please account for that state before defaulting to 0 and add a regression test covering `SELECT` followed by another command.

replies.body:
This is a pre-existing limitation rather than a regression from defaulting to 0, and it is deliberately out of scope for this change, which only concerns the value 0. This instrumentation never tracks Vert.x's tainted-connection state, so it already reports the URI's configured database regardless of any runtime `SELECT`. A connection opened with `redis://host:port/1` and then switched with `SELECT 2` already reports database 1 for later commands today, before this change. Defaulting the no-`select` case to 0 just extends that same existing behavior to the default database instead of leaving it absent, which is what matches the Vert.x client's own view of an untainted connection (its `CommandReporter` reports `"0"` when `uri.select()` is null and the connection is not tainted).

Fixing the tainted-state case would mean teaching the javaagent to track `isTainted()` for every connection, which is a separate change that affects the already-selected case as well, not just database 0. The PR description already calls this gap out as pre-existing and out of scope, so I'm leaving it here and not adding tainted-state tracking or the `SELECT`-then-command regression test in this PR.
